reason: A opens with a dramatized scene — the water-clock, the bronze disks, the exchange with Meletus — that pulls a general reader in before any definitional work begins, and it varies its material (courtroom, Neolithic houses, mass graves, the Old Bailey) so each section feels like new ground. B's Chicago section is vivid but then the chapter settles into long, undifferentiated paragraphs of Roman legal exposition and repeated methodological cautions about what sources can and cannot tell us. B restates the evidence-limits point at least five times (paragraphs 3, 33, 35, 43, 47, 49), which drains the sense of movement; A makes the same point once at the end and keeps its middle moving through concrete cases.
